products.title: Next Generation Guard Passing by Mica Galvao
products.body:
Learn How To Destroy The Guard With Effective Modern Techniques From Up-And-Coming Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Phenom Mica Galvao’s Guide To Attacking The Guard

  • Mica Galvao shows you how he attacks the guard with knee cuts, submissions, and more with next-generation details and technical adaptations
  • Use this knee cut system to control the guard and slice your way through it as you master this common passing style
  • Combine submissions and back takes to attack from top and finish the fight with baseball chokes and brabo chokes
  • Use toreando and over under passes to combine movement and pressure into a crushing style


Learn How To Destroy The Guard With Effective Modern Techniques From Up-And-Coming Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Phenom Mica Galvao’s Guide To Attacking The Guard

Check out a free sample:

 

What Will You Learn?


Level up your guard passing and top game with techniques and concepts from one of the brightest prospects in all of Brazilian jiu-jitsu, as young phenom Mica Galvao teaches you how he attacks the guard. Use guard passes like knee cuts, toreando, over under, and more to create a unified passing style, supercharged with some of Mica’s tricky techniques to make every move as effective as possible.



Mica is one of BJJ’s most exciting young stars, and has built up win streaks of over 100 matches in his competitive career. This young brown belt has been studying and learning his entire life and now is ready to share these techniques with you.

Prevent The Deep Half

 


Pass the guard with modern variations of some of BJJ’s most common passes, including Mica’s knee cut system. Slide and slice through the guard as he shows you techniques that make passing the legs and controlling the head easier, as well as how to combine passes to mount and counters to reverse De La Riva.

Combine toreando and over under to combine movement and pressure passes, with Mica’s advice on how each style is needed and can work off one another.

products.title: Next Generation Closed Guard by Mica Galvao
products.body:
Fight From The Classic Closed Guard With Modern Upgrades From Next Generation Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Phenom Mica Galvao

  • Master the modern closed guard as grappling phenom Mica Galvao teaches you how the next generation is using this classic position
  • Secure strong grips and use 2 on 1’s and underhooks to work for submissions and sweeps that work at all levels
  • Sweep from bottom with the most powerful sweeps possible, including combos from flower sweeps, bump sweeps, mermaids, and more
  • Get to closed guard with some of the best ways to pull guard and secure your closed guard for safety and control


Fight From The Classic Closed Guard With Modern Upgrades From Next Generation Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Phenom Mica Galvao

Check out a free sample:

 

What Will You Learn?


The closed guard may be one of submission grappling’s most common and classic positions, with roots back to the start of Brazilian jiu-jitsu. Now, you can take that closed guard to the next generation with young phenom Mica Galvao’s instructional series on how he uses a modern closed guard to sweep and submit.



Mica is one of BJJ’s most exciting young stars, and has built up win streaks of over 100 matches in his competitive career. This young brown belt has been studying and learning his entire life and now is ready to share these techniques with you.

Check Out Mica's Balao Sweep

 


Grip to 2 on 1’s and underhooks that can win you upper body position and let you start launching attacks. Use armbars, back takes, triangles, and more to control the fight, upgrade position, and get the submission. Mica shows you how he uses flower sweeps and bump sweeps to work in combinations, and how you can too.

Consistently Work Your Way To The Guard!

products.title: Galvao Style Back Attacks by Mica Galvao
products.body:
Find the back from everywhere and learn the most effective ways to finish the fight with Mica’s help and careful coaching

  • Mica Galvao is one of grappling’s greatest phenoms ever, establishing himself as a black belt world champion and elite competitor before even turning 20!
  • Take the back from turtle position and see the best ways to maintain control with the hips and grips available to you
  • Pass your way to the back with Mica’s combinations and techniques from leg drags, toreando, double unders, half guard, and more
  • Finish fights more often with step-by-step breakdowns of how to do bow and arrows, paper cutters, rear naked chokes, triangles, and more!

2022 Black Belt World Champion Mica Galvao Shows His Entire System For Finding Back Control And Finishing Fights So Students Of All Levels Can Learn How To Get The Most Dominant Position In Grappling With Ease

Check out a free sample:

What Will You Learn?

Win fights in the most dominant and effective way possible, as black belt World Champion and rising superstar Mica Galvao teaches his system for taking the back and securing chokes. With this 4-part series, you can see all the ways that Mica has been perfecting and using in competition as he has risen through the ranks, with advice that will help students of all levels improve their offensive arsenal.

Mica Galvao has already established himself as one of the best black belt competitors on Earth, having won a world championship before the age of 20. Now you can start to see how he has developed his game so quickly, by focusing his game on effective fight-ending offense that cuts through defenses with systematic progress.

Learn how to take the back in stages with Mica’s techniques for securing maximum control, including how he’s made a successful run by finding the back through guard passing. Combine your double unders, leg drags, half guard, and more with back takes that will give you a great opportunity to finish the fight.

Secure that final tap with multiple options as Mica shows how he sets up chokes with and without the lapel. See how to apply successful zipper chokes, paper cutters, rear naked chokes, and more, so that you can cycle through until you get that final tap from your opposition.
